text:
Alex Chen: Quick proposal — thinking about a lightweight 'gateway shim' pattern for internal API surface. Instead of a big central HTTP gateway doing JSON <-> gRPC translation, each service gets a tiny shim that exposes a REST-ish edge and forwards as gRPC to the service. Goals: let services own their surface, keep backend gRPC semantics, reduce central gateway complexity. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

Maria V: Do you mean a per-service sidecar shim or a shared shim cluster in front of many services?

Alex Chen: Per-service sidecar is the initial idea — small process (or envoy filter) that handles translation, validation, and a bit of auth-to-mTLS mapping. Pros: team ownership, incremental rollouts. Cons: duplication of translation logic and more deployables.

Samir Rao: Major concern is telemetry and quotas. If we push translation to sidecars, how do we keep quotas/alerts consistent in Console? We still need a central place to enforce global limits.

Jin Park: Agreed. One option: shim emits standardized labels/metrics and calls a lightweight policy service for quota checks (sync call on request). Adds a hop though — tail latency impact.

Maria V: Latency is sensitive for inference routes. Adding a policy RPC could add ~5-20ms. Could we use a local token-bucket with periodic sync to central policy to avoid per-request RPC?

Alex Chen: Sketch of a minimal proto for shim wrapper (very rough):
```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package api.shim;
message ShimRequest {
  string id = 1;
  bytes payload = 2;
  map<string, string> meta = 3;
}
```

Samir Rao: Also: auth. Shim needs to validate inbound bearer tokens and either mint mTLS identity or map to an internal service account. That mapping logic adds complexity and potential attack surface.

Jin Park: Alternative is central HTTP gateway that handles auth/quotas/translation and then routes to gRPC backends. Simpler for policy but single point for performance and rollout. Also harder to let teams iterate on API shape.

Maria V: Hybrid idea: edge layer (shared) performs auth + coarse quotas + rate-limiting; sidecar does translation, validation, and local caching for quotas and schema. Console aggregates metrics from both.

Alex Chen: Rollouts UX: plan is to support header-based canaries and a console toggle per-service to switch shim mode (on / off / passthrough). Need safe fallback to passthrough when schema drift occurs.

ops-bot: FYI — previous shim rollout caused a 0.4% error spike during schema drift (incident 2025-06-11). See incident runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2025-06-11

deploy-bot: Started canary rollout job #234 for api/shim v0.3 — 5% traffic to canary.

Samir Rao: I can prototype the token-bucket sync design and a k6 load test to measure tail latencies. Volunteers to pair on envoys/protos? @Jin Park?

Jin Park: I’ll take envoy config + proto stabilization. Also happy to run perf tests with the runtime team.

Maria V: I’ll add a small dashboard for shim metrics (translation failure rate, policy RPC latency, local bucket saturation) and a console control for canary percentage + fallback.

Alex Chen: Awesome — action items: Samir (token-bucket proto + perf tests), Jin (envoy + proto), Maria (console dashboards + rollout controls). Follow-up sync Friday 10:00am. Thanks everyone :tada:
